lesson.title: Intervals of Increase and Decrease
intro: A parabola changes direction at its vertex.
To the left of the vertex, a parabola may be increasing or decreasing.
To the right of the vertex, the behavior reverses.
An interval of increase describes where the function values get larger as \(x\) increases.

workedExample.problem: A parabola has a vertex at \((3,-2)\) and opens upward. Over what interval is it increasing?
steps: For an upward-opening parabola, the graph decreases to the vertex and increases after the vertex.
workedExample.aiHint: Check whether the parabola opens up or down, then look to the right of the vertex.

questions.prompt: A parabola is graphed on the set of axes below. Over which interval is the parabola only increasing?
questions.explanation: From the graph, the vertex is at \(x=3\), and the parabola opens upward, so it is increasing for \(x \ge 3\).
